teams.heading: Farrell says Ireland are raising the standard before Fiji, after 30-point win
teams.body: Friday night's win over Argentina moved Ireland top of the northern hemisphere table for at least 24 hours, and Ireland head coach Farrell said the aim is to keep improving in every area and to show the squad what is acceptable. "I suppose it's raising the standard to be as good as we possibly can," he said. The response followed a 40-21 defeat by the All Blacks at Eden Park. Fiji are next, in Round 5 of the Nations Championship.

lead.why: It is the only new item about Fiji's next opponent rather than a France match report or a France-focused story, and the other new items are already covered or belong to another team.

teams.heading: Furbank returns at full-back as Fin Smith passes fitness test for Australia
teams.body: England's Fin Smith has been declared fit after a scare in the build-up, and George Furbank returns at full-back for the first time since November 2024, when injuries and a bout of appendicitis in the July window kept him out of the Test side. Smith has started each of England's past five outings at fly-half, usurping George Ford in the process. Greg Fisilau is in the match-day squad and could win his maiden Test cap off the bench.

lead.why: A fresh selection story with concrete personnel news (Smith's fitness, Furbank's return, a possible debutant) for the England side facing Australia.

teams.heading: France lose Romain Ntamack for rest of Nations Championship after shoulder injury
teams.body: Head coach Fabien Galthié confirmed to TF1 that Romain Ntamack will miss the rest of the Nations Championship after injuring his left shoulder during Saturday's 54-17 win over Fiji in Lyon. "Romain went off with this injury and we won't have him for the rest of the competition," Galthié said. Ntamack was forced off after just 34 minutes, and no recovery timetable has been announced pending further assessment. Matthieu Jalibert is also unavailable, so France must find a replacement at ten ahead of the South Africa test.

lead.why: A new injury to France's first-choice fly-half, ruled out for the rest of the Nations Championship, is the story a fan would text a mate about.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell wants Ireland 'more ruthless' despite six-try Argentina win
teams.body: Ireland coach Andy Farrell said there is still room for improvement after the 42-12 win over Argentina, despite six tries to two. "How we can be a little bit more ruthless because that's the team that we want to be," he said. Lock Tadhg Beirne agreed that some of the tries were proper team efforts but felt the side could have scored more. Fiji come next, before the world champion Springboks.

lead.why: Farrell's post-match verdict on the Argentina win is a fresh coach comment, distinct from the Keenan hat-trick and Casey selection stories already run.

teams.heading: Quesada credits Italy's forwards and maul defence after 66-7 Springboks loss
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada, speaking after the defeat in Turin, said his forwards had produced a performance of notable quality, pointing to closing out of phases and maul defence against a side hard to stop on the five-metre line. He said the kicking game and restarts did not work. Quesada added that Italy at times put themselves under pressure, but in the second half, up to the 70th minute, they had more ball and possession and scored a try.

lead.why: It is a new, official post-match briefing from Italy's head coach and captain, with the federation's own account of what went right and wrong, rather than a repeat of the result or a pundit's verdict.

teams.heading: Sione Tuipulotu takes 'full responsibility' for sin-binning in All Blacks defeat
teams.body: Captain Sione Tuipulotu said Scotland's discipline "wasn't good enough, and it starts with me" after the 43-21 defeat at Murrayfield. Moments after he was sin-binned on 50 minutes, Beauden Barrett scored his second try, with Scotland conceding 13 penalties to New Zealand's eight. Tuipulotu said they were "nowhere near accurate enough" in the second half, and described next week's Australia match as a must-win game.

lead.why: Scotland's captain publicly took responsibility for the discipline lapses behind the defeat, a new post-match development rather than a retelling of the match.

teams.heading: Warburton and Biggar urge Tandy against wholesale changes for All Blacks test
teams.body: Sam Warburton and Dan Biggar, speaking on ITV after the Japan win, want head coach Steve Tandy to keep changes limited for the All Blacks. Warburton said he favours Warren Gatland's approach, arguing that just because a performance has been "slightly underwhelming doesn't mean you make wholesale changes." He also suggested front-row changes could be considered, pointing to Rhys Carre, Ryan Elias and Tomas Francis, who came on after half-time and helped Wales gain ascendancy at scrum time. Carre, in particular, made a strong impact.

teams.heading: Efraín Elías yellow-carded as Pumas' forwards are disrupted in Dublin
teams.body: Efraín Elías was yellow-carded for a high tackle on Hugo Keenan, and Ireland's final try, a Rónan Kelleher lineout maul, came against a seven-man Pumas pack. Justo Piccardo had earlier been yellow-carded for offside, and Ireland led 21-5 at half-time. Ireland won the Aviva Stadium contest 42-12 on Friday, with Keenan's hat-trick completed on 49 minutes.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson urges Wallabies to 'play our own game' against England
teams.body: Ahead of the opener, Wilson said the Wallabies "definitely want to be us", pointing to the 42-38 win over South Africa in Perth in September, when they backed their skills and kept attacking. The captain said the two New Zealand defeats, where Australia conceded 93 points, had taught lessons that must be carried forward. Coach Les Kiss has warned that England's back three can do damage if given space, and does not expect a forward battle alone. England have lost five of their last seven Tests.

teams.heading: Mark Nawaqanitawase joins Saitama Wild Knights; coach Berrick Barnes hails arrival
teams.body: Japan club Saitama Wild Knights have welcomed Mark Nawaqanitawase, and backs and attack coach Berrick Barnes is delighted. "We're so lucky to have him," Barnes told AAP from just outside Tokyo. The former Wallabies vice-captain said Nawaqanitawase, who arrived on Thursday, already knew many of the squad's names and had watched footage of how the side plays. Barnes added that he is positive around the group and lifts the Japanese players up.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett becomes second All Black to reach 50 Test tries against Scotland
teams.body: Beauden Barrett's brace in the 43-21 win at Murrayfield on Saturday brought up his half-century of Test tries. Planet Rugby noted the tally also passed Doug Howlett's try-scoring tally. His 49th came earlier, from a Damian McKenzie flat pass after Peter Lakai was sent to the sin bin, and the 50th arrived two minutes after Josh Moorby's try.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus says Salmaan Moerat withdrew from Italy test with back spasms
teams.body: Salmaan Moerat, who was set to make his first Test appearance of 2026, was replaced at the last minute by Lood de Jager, with Franco Mostert moving onto the bench. Erasmus said Moerat had a minor issue on Thursday, looked good at the captain's run, then got more back spasms in the warm-up, and hoped it was not too serious. Moerat was the only casualty, Erasmus said, and he did not think there were other serious injuries.
